hook_text: Why did some British women in 1917 have bright yellow skin?
clip_script: They made shells. With millions of men at the front, about nine hundred thousand women worked in munitions factories by 1918, filling shells with TNT. The chemical turned their skin yellow, so they were called canaries. Explosions at Barnbow and Silvertown killed dozens. The pay was better than being a maid, and many loved their new freedom. Women also drove buses, worked farms and served in uniform. Then the war ended, and most were sent home.
visual_style: A whiteboard factory floor with women filling shells, a yellow tint spreading, then the factory gates closing in 1918.
pacing: Builds from the hook to the work to the aftermath.
